title: Judge validity vs human judgment — SummEval, pooled summary level (the strict read)
what_this_is: A machine-readable record of how well SUM's meaning-loss proxies track expert human judgments, at the STRICTEST aggregation level. It is evidence ABOUT the judge, published unsigned: calibration is a measurement of the instrument, not a certified property of any document.

corpus.name: SummEval (mteb/summeval, test split)
corpus.human_labels: expert annotations, 1-5 per axis; proxy target = meaning composite, loss = (5 - score)/4

aggregation_note: Per-summary rank correlation pooled across all systems and articles. 80.6% of SummEval consistency ratings sit at exactly 5.0/5, so range restriction compresses correlations at this level; published anchors on the same benchmark at this level: ROUGE 0.12-0.19, BERTScore 0.11, QuestEval 0.31, BARTScore 0.38, GPT-4 G-Eval 0.51.
scope_limits: Correlations at this aggregation level are MODEST (~0.27-0.33): the proxy is directionally valid, not a substitute for human judgment.
Measured on news summarization; transfer to other domains/transforms is NOT established by this card (see the FRANK cards for one out-of-domain replication).
These numbers must never ride in a signed receipt field: they were measured on this corpus with these judges, not on whatever corpus a receipt certifies.

See the companion system-level card: on the SAME data the system-level correlations are ~0.57-0.75 — the apparent conflict with published '0.6-class' numbers is aggregation level + corpus, not disagreement.
reading_guidance: Use this card to decide how much weight a meaning_risk bound deserves as evidence about MEANING (as opposed to its exact cryptographic/statistical content, which is corpus- and judge-specific and replayable from the receipt itself).
